frontier.hypothesis: Canonical-asm authorization under the GTE-leaf carve-out remains the disposition, and session 6 adds an affirmative provenance argument rather than one more null result.
frontier.mechanism: Forensics shows GCC CAN name $t0..$t7 for these eight values, but only from a register-pressure state costing >= 10 extra instructions (ctlE + ctlF), and CAN fill this jr's delay slot, but only when the candidate insn is not an asm (ctlA differential against reorg.c:730-735 stop_search_p). The target does both at once in exactly 17 instructions using an opcode (ctc2) with no C analog. Precedent is in hand and citable: func_80052B44, src/text1b.c:10995, inline_asm_canonical.txt:340, authorized 2026-07-27 for the identical construct one function later in the same file.
frontier.next_probe: A session or operator holding authority over inline_asm_canonical.txt applies memory/grind/func_80052B00/candidate.c over src/text1b.c:10969-10994, adds the canonical entry, runs `retire func_80052B00` (drops regfix.txt:3411) and `verify-oracle`. The disposition call belongs to the driver/owner; a grind session in a non-escalation modality must not self-authorize it.

frontier.hypothesis: If the canonical disposition is ever REFUSED, memory/grind/func_80052B00/best_pure_c_fused8_floor17.c - not the pinned HEAD body - is what should ship, because it strictly reduces the cheat surface.
frontier.mechanism: The HEAD body needs eight register asm("$N") pins PLUS regfix.txt:3411 to byte-match. The fused body is pin-free and already correct in opcodes, order and offsets; only the GPR names and the delay-slot move remain as build-time paperwork.
frontier.next_probe: Operator step (a grind session may not touch these surfaces): splice the fused body into src/text1b.c, measure `sandbox func_80052B00` WITHOUT --disable all to see what the enabled rule set achieves, determine the minimal rule set that reaches byte-match, and run a full `verify-oracle`.

frontier.hypothesis: The register axis should not be re-opened on the spelling dimension; the only untested corner left anywhere is zero-cost occupancy of $2,$3,$5,$6,$7, and it is four specific constructs, not a sweep.
frontier.mechanism: Six sessions measured the spelling dimension three independent ways (19 hand spellings, ~164k permuter iterations, and now the compiler's own reload/local-alloc dumps) and s6 identified the single lever that moves the register set together with the arithmetic excluding it. Unused parameters are killed; what remains untested is whether a $v0 return value, a DImode return occupying $v0+$v1, setjmp, or alloca can occupy those registers without emitting an instruction.
frontier.next_probe: One ctl sweep of those four constructs against the fused body with cc1 -da, reading only the .greg spill list - roughly one turn of work, and it closes the last theoretical gap in the register argument. Do NOT sweep C spellings again and do NOT run a fourth permuter campaign.
